evidence.note: Diagnosed -0.5-should-round-to--0.0 from a specific failing f32 nearest assertion, then fixed the zero-sign bug in BOTH runtime.rs and simd.rs — updated model and generalized the fix across files.
Hit an unreachable! panic in conversions; realized narrowing ops 0x85/0x86 were mis-classified as unary and corrected the classification rather than patching symptoms.

bitselect returning all-zeros: formed hypotheses about operand stack order, traced root cause to a stray empty 0x52 match arm shadowing the real implementation, removed it, verified with temporary debug prints then cleaned them up.
assert_invalid failure led to realizing memory alignment cannot exceed natural size; generalized the alignment check across SimdLoad/Store/Lane at once.

Removed single-table/memory constraint at root to unblock several suites, then later reinstated the multiple-memories check when memory.json required it — revising an over-broad earlier correction across the long horizon.

trunc float-to-int conversions took several boundary edits, each with a new hypothesis (NaN vs overflow, f32→f64 precision, exact math bounds) — genuine progressive refinement but with a guess-and-check float-boundary flavor, the weakest adaptation in the run.

reasoning: Across the trajectory the agent repeatedly reads failing-assertion detail, diagnoses the underlying wrong model (sign handling, unary/binary misclassification, shadowed match arm, alignment/lane-index rules, trap messages), updates the implementation, and generalizes fixes across a family and even across files while re-running the family and full suite to confirm — matching the level-8 anchor. It even performs root-level course correction (removing then reinstating table/memory constraints). It falls short of 10 because the recurring trunc-conversion boundary problem was resolved through several fiddly guess-and-check iterations rather than one systematic model fix, and there was no single recognition of a shared cross-family assumption fixed at the root.
